base_sample_collapse.explanation: batch_range=(0,-2) makes _get_collapsed_shape set every t-batch dim to 1, so the SAME standard normals are reused for every candidate t-batch element -> the score cannot depend on chunking or on a candidate's position in the batch.

cells_vs_inclusion_exclusion.note: Cross-checks the q=1 cell-decomposition formula against HVI = prod(y) - HV({min(y,p)}) computed by inclusion-exclusion with no botorch in the path.

fixed_posterior_no_gp.note: exact (non-log) qNEHVI over a fixed float64 mean/var table

gp_predict_call_shape.interpretation: The Tanimoto Gram is bitwise chunk-invariant; the float32 posterior solve downstream of it is NOT. So the chunk dependence lives in the GP's float32 linear algebra, not in the sampler.
gp_predict_call_shape.note: mogp.predict on the EXACT (chunk*(B+1), n_fp) matrix DockingPosteriorModel builds, i.e. row counts 325/325/325/169/91/13.

current_impl_log_qnehvi.note: These are LOG values. The global torch RNG state at call time selects the Sobol seed, so the acquisition value is not a function of (run_seed, iteration) alone.

decomposition_scaling.note: K (cell count) for a seeded uniform front of size B in 5-D. K is deterministic; the wall-clock is in capture_runtime.txt because a timing is not byte-reproducible. B grows every BO iteration (n_init + batch*iteration), so this -- not N -- is the scaling risk.

legacy_main_fixture_ties.fixture: acquisition.py __main__ verbatim: np.random.seed(0), torch.manual_seed(0), 12 baseline / 25 candidates, 5% random bits, train_mogp(n_iterations=50). Bounds/signs/ref forced to the repo's evaluation frame.

log_vs_exact.note: The log variant is a different (smoothed) estimator, so this is an ORDER comparison only; the values are not commensurable.

numpy_chunk_invariance.note: The numpy reference estimator must be BITWISE chunk-invariant. The shipped torch path is not (see chunk_sweep).

problem_small25.note: GP hyperparameters are FIXED, never trained; predict() is pure.

real_library_pool.caveats: Real fingerprints and real known-exact ADMET. The docking targets that train the baseline GP are synthetic (the library is not docked up front), the GP hyperparameters are fixed, and the pool is the raw cached library WITHOUT the heavy-atom floor and quality screen load_library() applies. This isolates the acquisition layer, not the GP and not the library build.

reduction_order_synthetic.note: numpy reduces a 2-D array along axis 0 row by row, so mean(axis=0) and a streaming accumulator agree bitwise -- EXCEPT when Mc == 1, where numpy switches to pairwise summation over a contiguous vector.

reference_vs_botorch_same_normals.interpretation: Fed the SAME standard normals, the numpy reference estimator and botorch's exact qNEHVI must agree to float64 round-off. This is the estimator-layer differential test.

splice.interpretation: Under the DIAGONAL posterior the spliced and decoupled estimators share an expectation, so the measured gap is MC noise, not bias. The splice is still mandatory: it is the definition of NEHVI and the only version that stays correct if the covariance ever stops being diagonal.
